defect.description: services/telemetry/test_capture.py imported `capture` and services/telemetry/test_feedback_adapter.py imported `feedback_adapter` and `capture` as bare top-level modules. Those names only resolve when sys.path[0] is services/telemetry, so repository-root unittest discovery replaced both modules with unittest.loader._FailedTest placeholders.
defect.impact: Two loader errors on every repository-root discovery run, and 75 telemetry tests that never executed while the suite still reported a total. Silent loss of coverage, not merely a red count.
defect.root_cause: Bare sibling imports inside a package that has __init__.py at both services/ and services/telemetry/, executed with the repository root rather than the service directory as the first sys.path entry.

repair.description: Both modules import through services.telemetry.capture and services.telemetry.feedback_adapter. No sys.path bootstrap was added: the package path is sufficient under repository-root unittest discovery, under python -m unittest services.telemetry.<module>, and under pytest prepend import mode, and avoiding the insert avoids a process-global side effect that would leak into other modules loaded in the same discovery run.
repair.production_behavior_unchanged: capture.py and feedback_adapter.py are byte-identical to their f9b6760d6 versions. The 75 recovered tests are the modules' own pre-existing assertions, executed unmodified; only the import lines changed.

regression_fence.description: services/telemetry/test_discovery_imports.py asserts the import contract for the whole package rather than the two specific call sites.
regression_fence.recursion_guard: Child interpreters carry PANTHEON_TELEMETRY_DISCOVERY_IMPORT_CHILD=1; the subprocess-spawning test class skips when that sentinel is set, so a widened discovery pattern cannot fork recursively.
tests: test_no_telemetry_test_module_imports_a_bare_package_sibling — AST scan of every services/telemetry/test_*.py; no import whose root name is a telemetry package sibling. Explicit relative imports remain allowed.
test_repaired_modules_import_siblings_through_the_package_path — the two repaired modules import via services.telemetry.*.
test_repaired_modules_do_not_mutate_process_global_sys_path — AST scan; neither repaired module touches sys.path.
test_repaired_modules_discover_with_zero_loader_errors — in-process TestLoader().discover with top_level_dir at the repository root yields zero _FailedTest and exactly 75 tests.
test_repeated_discovery_in_one_process_is_stable — repeated discovery in one interpreter gives identical, error-free results.
test_importing_repaired_modules_leaves_no_bare_sibling_in_sys_modules — no bare capture / feedback_adapter alias is registered, so the duplicate-module-identity hazard is closed too.
test_repo_root_discovery_of_repaired_modules_reports_no_loader_error — subprocess repository-root discovery under a scrubbed environment.
test_repaired_modules_run_from_a_foreign_working_directory — both modules run with cwd set to a temporary directory.

test_repaired_modules_import_under_hostile_ambient_environment — import succeeds with hostile PANTHEON_RUNTIME_MANAGER_* values, INCIDENTS_DATA_DIR, and a nonexistent PYTHONPATH prefix, leaking no sibling alias.
test_repaired_modules_collect_under_pytest_from_a_foreign_cwd — pytest --collect-only from a foreign cwd collects all 75 tests; skips when pytest is absent.
